correctness.rationale: For the operator \(K e_n=\frac{1}{n+1}e_{n+1}\), finite-rank truncations converge in norm and the exact formula \(\|K^m\|=1/m!\) proves compactness and quasinilpotence. For any unilateral weighted shift with all weights nonzero, a commuting nonzero \(A\) has a first nonzero coordinate in \(Ae_0\); the corresponding first nonzero coordinate of \(Ax\) cannot cancel for a vector \(x\) with a first nonzero coordinate. Thus \(A\) is injective. If non-scalar \(S\) commuting with \(K\) had an eigenvalue \(\lambda\), then \(S-\lambda I\) would be a nonzero noninjective member of the commutant. Finally, any operator commuting with a nonzero rank-one operator has an eigenvector. These implications contradict a chain \(K\leftrightarrow S\leftrightarrow F\).
